fix.notes: The fix is scoped exactly to the case where normalize_version reduces the entire name to a bare version token. No other code paths are affected. The pattern ^v\d[\.\d]*$ is conservative and mirrors what normalize_version produces.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

When a deck is named something like `version 2`, `normalize_version` correctly converts it to `v2`. However, because the resulting name is non-empty, `add_colors_if_no_deck_name`, `normalize_colors`, and `add_archetype_if_just_colors` all skip over it — treating `v2` as a real deck name rather than an empty one. The deck ends up named `v2` instead of something meaningful like `Mono Blue Aggro v2`.

## What changed

In `decksite/deck_name.py`, after `normalize_version`, added a check for whether the result is a bare version marker (`^v\d[\.\d]*$`). If so, the version suffix is saved, the name is blanked, the color/archetype logic runs on the blank name as usual, and then the version suffix is appended to the result.

Updated the corresponding test in `decksite/deck_name_test.py` at line 246 to expect `'Mono Blue Aggro v2'` instead of `'v2'`.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed
- `uv run --frozen pytest decksite/deck_name_test.py -v` — 326 passed
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit decksite/deck_name_test.py` — 845 passed, 1 skipped

Fixes #12144
